learningObjective: Define TTFT precisely and use timeline data to diagnose which phase drives it.

canonicalClaims.claim: TTFT is the wall-clock time from request arrival to delivery of the first output token; for long prompts on batch-1 it is typically dominated by the prefill phase.
conditions: Streaming output (first token delivered as soon as available).
nonImplications: Does not describe generation latency; total latency includes all decode steps.
Does not equal TPOT / inter-token latency.

misconceptions.claim: TTFT is the average inter-token latency of the decode phase.
misconceptions.whyWrong: That is TPOT; TTFT is the latency until the first token.
TTFT covers queue + tokenize + prefill + first-token generation.

misconceptions.claim: Reducing prefill always reduces TTFT proportionally.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Under load, queueing can dominate; reducing prefill has diminishing returns.

implementationFacts: Chunked prefill breaks the prompt into pieces to interleave with other requests' decode steps.
Prefix caching skips prefill for shared prefixes (system prompts, few-shot examples).
performanceScenarios: Long-context prompts (thousands of tokens) make prefill the dominant TTFT contributor.
Under high load, queueing can rival prefill for TTFT dominance.
